responsibility: Implements the main C-side backend for GCC’s TILEPro port. This file owns most target hooks and helper routines for ABI and calling convention decisions, supported scalar/vector modes, argument passing and return values, varargs handling, address legitimacy and constant handling, builtin registration and expansion, register and frame usage, instruction costs and scheduling/reorg support, multiply-by-constant expansion support, trampoline and thunk emission, operand/address printing, profiling output, and final assembler/file hooks; it consumes the machine-description interfaces from tilepro.h/tilepro.md and installs them through the targetm TARGET_INITIALIZER definitions.
same_name_distinction: Unlike the sibling tilepro.h header, tilepro.md machine description, and tilepro.opt option table, this is the executable C++ backend implementation file that defines TILEPro target hook functions and helper routines, then binds them into GCC via TARGET_* macros and targetm. It provides the procedural logic that uses interfaces declared in the header and cooperates with patterns from the .md file, rather than declaring machine macros, RTL patterns, or command-line options.
